newsitem.title: USA: US Spot Prods--USG gasoline rebounds, NYH gains.
newsitem.headline: US Spot Prods--USG gasoline rebounds, NYH gains.

text.p: U.S. Gulf conventional gasoline differentials rebounded from a modest dip early as tight market conditions kept prompt barrels near the August NYMEX level.
But traders were loathe to link Gulf gasoline's strength to a refinery unit outage in Louisiana, though they were not willing to dismiss the outage's bullish effects either.
New York Harbor gasoline differentials also gained, led by the strength in the premium grades, while Midcontinent levels were steady to slightly weaker.
On NYMEX, August gasoline was up 0.52 cent at 58.75 cents a gallon and August heating oil was down 0.25 cent at 52.40 cents a gallon.
U.S. GULF
Buying interest for conventional gasoline re-emerged in early afternoon trading, according to market watchers, erasing the modest dip made in the morning.

Prompt regular conventional M1 gasoline was offered at about even with the August NYMEX but appeared to be firming going into the NYMEX close. Prices at the August screen were steady with late Wednesday levels but nearly 0.50 cent up from the bottom reached this morning.
Conventional M1 differentials have gained about 2.0 cents from early this week, traders said, on a combination of refiner and trader buying, players said.

Market watcters said news that Mobil had shut a 20,000 barrel-per-day hydrocracker after a fire Wednesday at its Chalmette, Louisiana refinery may have lent some strength to the market, though little real supply disruption should be felt.
NEW YORK HARBOR
Premium gasoline was all the rage in the Harbor Thursday afternoon as tightness in markets for octane enhancers like aromatics and MTBE began to spill over into gasoline markets.
"The premiums are just screaming," said one trader.

While no premium deals could be immediately confirmed, prompt "V2" conventional 93-octane premium unleaded was heard offered a cent firmer than differentials on Wednesday at 6.75 cents over August futures.
Differentials on prompt "D2" 93-octane reformulated advanced about half a cent to between 7.25 and 7.50 cents over.

The regular 87-octane blends were also about 0.15 to 0.30 cent firmer than in morning action, with prompt "A2" reformulated blend heard done at 0.50 cent over August futures, while "M2" conventional firmed to 1.75 cent under.
The distillates in the Harbor remained relatively quiet compared to gasoline, traders said.
MIDCONTINENT

Markets were little changed in the Midcontinent in afternoon trade. Prompt Group Three unleaded gasoline differentials were pegged at 3.00/3.25 cents over August futures, with any months done at 2.25 cents.
Chicago prompt unleaded gasoline differentials were a tad lower at 2.50/3.00 cents, and the any months at about 1.75/2.00 cents.
Players said they saw some refiner demand in both hubs but the focus was on August barrels of gasoline.
The distillate side was also largely steady. Prompt low sulphur in Group Three was done at 2.60 over August futures and 2.35 cents over the print traded hands for any month barrels.
-- New York Oil Desk 1 212 859 1633
